Fri Nov 6policy

Trump names Stephen Miller White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles

President Donald Trump said Friday that Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff starting Nov. 9, days after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterms, AP, NBC News and NPR reported.

Fri Nov 6policy

Schumer says Democrats will block a right-wing Supreme Court nominee

Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats will not confirm a right-wing Supreme Court nominee or what he called "crappy nominees" to lower courts or the Cabinet after winning a Senate majority of at least 54 seats, AP, The Guardian and NBC News reported.

Thu Nov 5elections

Alaska and Mississippi Senate races still uncalled as Democrats hold at least 54 seats

Senate contests in Alaska and Mississippi remained uncalled on Thursday, leaving open whether Democrats will expand a majority of at least 54 seats after the midterms, AP and other outlets reported.

Thu Nov 5policy

Democrats say they will use new majorities to investigate Trump and his administration

After winning control of the House and Senate in the midterms, Democratic leaders said they plan major oversight investigations of President Donald Trump, his family and administration, AP, NPR and Politico reported.

Wed Nov 4elections

Democrats win majorities in both the House and Senate in the midterm elections

Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, with a Senate majority of at least 54 seats and a House majority secured early Wednesday, according to race calls reported by AP and Reuters.

Wed Nov 4elections

Democrats flip governor's offices in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Iowa; Becerra wins in California

Democrats won governor's races in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Iowa, taking offices held by Republicans, and Democrat Xavier Becerra was elected governor of California, AP, Reuters and NPR reported.

Wed Nov 4politics

Trump says Iran war 'largely' explains Republican losses; Speaker Johnson won't lead House GOP next year

President Donald Trump said Wednesday that Vice President JD Vance's view that the Iran war cost Republicans in the midterms was "largely true," while saying he would make the same decision again, NBC News and Reuters reported.

Wed Nov 4elections

Voters back abortion-rights measures in Nevada and Virginia, add photo ID rules and reject Missouri's new congressional map

Voters approved constitutional amendments protecting abortion rights in Nevada and Virginia, added photo ID requirements to the constitutions of Ohio, North Carolina and Nevada, and blocked a Republican-drawn congressional map in Missouri, NBC News and NPR reported.

Mon Nov 2elections

Justice Department asks Supreme Court to order California to set aside about 20,000 disputed ballots

The Justice Department on Monday asked the Supreme Court for emergency relief requiring California to set aside mail ballots from about 20,000 people the administration says may not be citizens, after a district judge and a 9th Circuit panel rejected the request, CBS News and NPR reported.

Mon Nov 2courts

Judge dismisses case against two ex-FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden probe

U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui in Washington on Monday dismissed the Justice Department's criminal complaint against former FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, finding no probable cause that they lied to Congress in 2023, NPR, CBS News and NBC News reported.

Mon Nov 2courts

Former Chicago FBI chief sues Patel, Blanche and U.S. attorney, saying he was forced out over 'Broadview Six' case

Douglas DePodesta, who led the FBI's Chicago field office until July, filed a federal lawsuit Monday alleging that U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros falsely blamed him for the collapse of the "Broadview Six" protest prosecution, leading to his forced resignation, CBS Chicago and the Chicago Sun-Times reported.

Sun Nov 1elections

Sen. Chris Murphy hospitalized after stroke, office says

Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut had a stroke on Saturday and is receiving treatment at Johns Hopkins, his office said on Sunday.

Sat Oct 31courts

Judge dismisses Trump's $10 billion suit against The Wall Street Journal for good

A federal judge in Miami on Saturday dismissed with prejudice President Donald Trump's refiled $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over a story on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

Fri Oct 30elections

Appeals court rejects Justice Department bid to set aside disputed California ballots

A 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals panel ruled 2-1 on Friday against the Justice Department's emergency request to have California set aside mail ballots from about 20,000 people the administration says may not be citizens, CBS News and Courthouse News reported.

Fri Oct 30courts

Judge opens inquiry into whether government lawyers misled the court in D.C. golf course case

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes said Friday she will examine whether Justice Department and Interior Department officials and lawyers misled the court or broke ethics rules in the case over changes to Washington's East Potomac golf course, CBS News and The Hill reported.

Fri Oct 30courts

Judge weighs Comey's bid to dismiss third case; prosecutors say they are still seeking an indictment

Lawyers for former FBI Director James Comey argued in federal court Friday that the Justice Department's latest case against him is time-barred, while a department lawyer said prosecutors are still presenting evidence to a grand jury; U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden did not rule, CBS News and NBC News reported.

Fri Oct 30elections

Pope Leo XIV votes by mail in U.S. midterms, Vatican says

Pope Leo XIV has submitted a mail-in ballot in Chicago for the U.S. midterm elections, the Holy See Press Office said Friday, making him the first pope to vote in a U.S. election, according to CBS News and AP.

Thu Oct 29elections

Judge rejects Justice Department bid to have California set aside about 20,000 ballots; DOJ appeals

U.S. District Judge David O. Carter on Wednesday denied the Justice Department's emergency request to make California segregate the ballots of roughly 20,000 people the administration says are likely noncitizens, writing that it would "wreak havoc" on an election already underway.

Thu Oct 29elections

Alaska governor orders state inquiry into recruitment of a second 'Dan Sullivan' Senate candidate

Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy said Thursday he has directed the state Department of Public Safety to investigate whether an effort to recruit a Senate candidate sharing incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan's name broke state law, after a New York Times report tied the effort to Democrat Mary Peltola's campaign.

Thu Oct 29courts

CNN, MS NOW and Politico expand lawsuit over White House press pool exclusions

CNN, MS NOW and Politico on Wednesday amended their lawsuit against the White House, asking a federal court for a permanent order and alleging the administration keeps excluding them from Oval Office and Air Force One press pool assignments because of their coverage.

Wed Oct 28courts

Judge blocks administration's $20 million government-funded ad campaign in DNC lawsuit

U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan in Washington on Wednesday issued a temporary restraining order barring the Office of Management and Budget and the Department of Homeland Security from developing or airing a set of government-funded ads, granting a request from the Democratic National Committee.

Wed Oct 28policy

Pentagon tells Congress the Iran war has cost $47.1 billion

The Defense Department estimated that the war with Iran had cost $47.1 billion as of Oct. 16, up about $3.5 billion from its previous estimate through Sept. 3, according to a document provided to Congress and reported by Stars and Stripes, CBS News and AP.

Wed Oct 28courts

Judge rules Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles

Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright ruled Tuesday that Bill Essayli is unlawfully serving as the de facto U.S. attorney in Los Angeles and disqualified him from overseeing two criminal cases, but delayed the order while the Justice Department seeks a stay pending appeal.

Tue Oct 27courts

Former FBI Director James Comey charged in a third federal case over 2016 disclosure

Federal prosecutors have charged former FBI Director James Comey with transmitting national defense information and conspiracy, according to a court filing unsealed Monday in Washington, the third criminal case brought against him since President Donald Trump returned to office.

Tue Oct 27elections

Appeals court sends Justice Department's bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots back to trial judge

A federal appeals court on Monday dismissed the Justice Department's emergency appeal over about 20,000 California ballots it is challenging, sending the dispute back to U.S. District Judge David O. Carter, who heard arguments Tuesday afternoon.

Tue Oct 27courts

Judge strikes Justice Department's overnight charges against two former FBI officials

A federal magistrate judge in Washington on Tuesday struck an unsigned, unsworn amended complaint that the Justice Department filed overnight against former FBI officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, which added an obstruction charge without a judge's review.

Tue Oct 27courts

Judge extends block on changes to D.C.'s East Potomac golf course; Trump says administration will appeal

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a preliminary injunction barring the Trump administration from cutting more trees at Washington's East Potomac Park without a court order and requiring 10 business days' notice before closing or permanently altering the park, and President Donald Trump said the administration will appeal.

Tue Oct 27politics

Rep. Thomas Massie says he will force House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Hegseth week of Nov. 9

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., said Monday he plans to force a House vote during the week of Nov. 9 on his resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth if Hegseth is still in office, Roll Call and The Hill reported.

Mon Oct 26courts

Judge rules Justice Department unlawfully fired prosecutor Maurene Comey

U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman ruled Monday that the Justice Department's July 2025 firing of former federal prosecutor Maurene Comey, daughter of former FBI Director James Comey, was unlawful, and granted her retroactive reinstatement and back pay.

Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · Politics Digest · elections

Justice Department sues to block Alaska Senate certification if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses

The lawsuit, filed Thursday in federal court in Alaska and signed by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward, argues that some supporters of the incumbent "likely will inadvertently vote for Daniel J. Sullivan," according to NBC News. It seeks to block certification pending an investigation into whether those votes were meant for the senator, the AP reported. "I'm the one that said do it," Trump told reporters Friday. Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday that it is not the department's intention to improperly interfere with certification.

Alaska election officials removed Daniel J. Sullivan from the ballot in June, but the state's courts, including the Alaska Supreme Court, ruled he could stay on. A Justice Department statement called his candidacy "frivolous" and cited the National Voter Registration Act. Democratic nominee Mary Peltola criticized the suit on X, and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee called it a "sham lawsuit." Daniel J. Sullivan has said he decided to run on his own.

Why it matters: Both parties expect a close race, and Alaska's ranked choice count can take weeks. Notre Dame law professor Derek Muller told the AP that the statute does not let the department block certification and that a court would likely dismiss the case next month if it is not made moot.
